s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays
salient_findings: Marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres with atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere
key_facts: Age of onset of seizures: 3 months
Seizures are progressively more frequent despite antiepileptic therapy
Delayed motor and cognitive milestones
Gradual behavioral changes, including disturbed sleep, irritability, and episodes of aimless talking
No family history of neurological disorders
No reported perinatal complications or trauma
Significant cognitive impairment and marked left hemiparesis with brisk reflexes
Electroencephalography showed focal abnormal brain activity
Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres with significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere

shortlist.label: Rasmussen encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with seizures and hemiparesis

shortlist.label: Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Cerebral hemiatrophy and seizures with developmental delays

shortlist.label: Hemimegalencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: Seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays with cerebral asymmetry

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Seizures, hemiparesis, and developmental delays with possible cerebral atrophy

shortlist.label: Cerebral hemiatrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Marked asymmetry of cerebral hemispheres with significant atrophy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of seizures, delayed motor and cognitive milestones, and significant cognitive impairment, along with the imaging findings of marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres with significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere and compensatory changes such as calvarial thickening and hyperpneumatization of the sphenoid bone and mastoid air cells, are consistent with Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome, which is characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy, often with a history of perinatal or early childhood insult, though the absence of reported perinatal complications or trauma does not rule out this diagnosis as the insult could have been minor or not recognized.

rejected.label: Rasmussen encephalitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with more rapid progression of neurological deficits and often with a more pronounced inflammatory component on imaging, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Hemimegalencephaly
rejected.why: Characterized by an overgrowth of one cerebral hemisphere, which is the opposite of the atrophy seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with a port-wine stain and leptomeningeal angiomatosis, which are not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Cerebral hemiatrophy
rejected.why: While this term describes the imaging findings, it is not a specific diagnosis but rather a feature that can be seen in several conditions, including Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome, making the latter a more specific and appropriate diagnosis given the clinical context.
